10.1002_adfm.75576: Electrolyte‐gated synaptic transistors (EGSTs) have emerged as promising neuromorphic devices capable of modulating synaptic weights via ion‐mediated control. However, the correlations between ion–polymer interactions and ion‐doping retention characteristics remain poorly understood. Notably, strategies that simultaneously control ion–polymer interactions and synaptic retention via electrolyte ions as independent design variables remain underexplored. In this study, we demonstrate that hydrogen‐bond‐mediated anion–polymer interactions play a central role in governing synaptic retention. Anions with asymmetric charge distribution give rise to strengthened hydrogen‐bond interactions, which regulate ion dynamics and suppress ion back‐diffusion. This hydrogen‐bond interaction effectively transforms ion relaxation behavior from a diffusion‐dominated to an interaction‐stabilized regime within the organic semiconductor. As a result, the devices exhibit enhanced synaptic retention together with excellent linearity during long‐term potentiation/depression (LTP/D). These findings provide molecular insight into hydrogen‐bond‐mediated synaptic retention in EGSTs, offering a mechanistic basis for the rational optimization of ion‐driven neuromorphic devices.
10.1021_acs.langmuir.6c05306: The nanoarchitectonic fabrication of multifunctional heterostructures that synergistically integrate photocatalytic environmental detoxification with electrochemical energy storage exemplifies an emerging frontier toward sustainable materials chemistry. Herein, a phytogenic-derived NiCo2O4/g-C3N4@rGO ternary heterostructure was synthesized to regulate electronic configuration, structural defects, and charge carrier transport through Ni/Co–O bonding and M–O–C interactions. The spectral and structural analyses revealed homogeneously distributed nanoparticles with an average crystallite size of ∼ 70 nm, a mesoporous heterostructure possessing a high specific surface area of 75.4 m2 g–1, a high defect density (nD = 1.74 × 1011 cm–2), a narrow optical bandgap (1.10 eV), and strong interfacial bonding with negative surface potential (ζ = −41.3 mV). Under natural solar radiation, the optimized heterostructure achieved 97% (4-NP), 96% (3-AP), and 92% (2,4-DNP) degradation of recalcitrant phenols, along with 71–81% total organic carbon (TOC) mineralization, subsequent pseudo-first-order kinetics, and stable activity over seven consecutive cycles. Statistical optimization via Box–Behnken design (BBD) recognized high predictive fidelity (R2 = 0.99), while GC–MS analysis elucidated a mineralization pathway primarily involving •OH and O2•– radicals. Electrochemical measurements revealed a pronounced supercapacitive response with dominant-diffusion contribution and enhanced surface contribution from corresponding individual components, with a specific capacitance of 1706 F g–1 at 4 A g–1 and significantly reduced charge-transfer resistance (Rct = 0.65 Ω), indicating improved accessibility of electroactive sites and favorable interfacial charge-transfer characteristics. The bifunctional heterostructure provides a promising platform for integrating various interfacial catalytic conversions with energy storage toward environmental remediation and energy conversion in the future.
10.1021_acsami.5c22128: High-loading electrodes are particularly crucial for the practical application of Na-ion batteries (NIBs) in large-scale energy storage systems. To enable high-power long-lifetime NIBs, cathode materials with rapid Na-ion diffusion and structural stability must be developed. In this study, a novel vanadium-based phosphate heterostructure cathode material of Na 8 V 5 (P 2 O 7 ) 2.925 (PO 4 ) 3.75 (N 8 VPP) was synthesized by the spray-drying method with a unique dual-phase heterostructure comprising Na 7 V 4 (P 2 O 7 ) 4 (PO 4 ) and Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 in a molar ratio of 0.725:1. The P 2 O 7 4– /PO 4 3– polyanionic hybrid heterostructure shows a pronounced increase in the number of electronic states near the Fermi level. This resulting electronic feature lowers the Na + migration energy barrier and promotes charge transfer, as confirmed by density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Under high-loading conditions (10 mg cm –2 ), the N 8 VPP cathode delivers remarkable capacities of 90.51 mAh g –1 and 41.88 mAh g –1 at 0.1 A g –1 and 10 A g –1, respectively. Additionally, the capacity retention ratio is 71.8% with 64.3 mAh g –1 after 1000 cycles at 2 A g –1, demonstrating excellent cycling stability and power capability. Furthermore, a Na-ion full battery of N 8 VPP//NaTi 2 (PO 4 ) 3 achieves an excellent capacity and outstanding cycling life of 73 mAh g –1 at 5 A g –1 and 3000 cycles at 2 A g –1, respectively. This study offers key design insights for high-performance N 8 VPP cathodes toward practical sodium-ion energy storage.
